key_insight: Small, efficient vision-language models trained with interval + natural-language rationale supervision can reliably detect and explain anomalies in time-series data, delivering competitive accuracy with far lower compute and improved trustworthiness.
problem_solved: Existing large multimodal models struggle to find and justify anomalous patterns in sequential data because benchmarks lack natural-language rationales and models are too large/inefficient for practical deployment.
method: Create VisAnomBench: a time-series anomaly benchmark that augments interval annotations with human-written natural-language rationales to ground explanations.

Train a tiny vision–language reasoning pipeline: convert time series to visual representations (plots/heatmaps), use lightweight multimodal adapters for fusion, and fine-tune the VLM to emit anomaly labels plus textual rationales.
Incorporate trust mechanisms during training and inference (rationale supervision, uncertainty calibration and contrastive/auxiliary tasks) to improve interpretability and confidence estimation.
impact: Enables practical, interpretable anomaly detection on resource-constrained devices and makes model decisions more auditable for analysts — reducing cost and increasing adoption of multimodal approaches in time-series monitoring.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: time-series → visualization → tiny VLM (fusion + adapter) → anomaly label + rationale
Before/after example: raw signal with highlighted anomalous interval and generated natural-language rationale
Model footprint chart: accuracy vs. model size/latency comparing tiny VLM to large baselines
Trust metrics panel: calibration curve or reliability diagram alongside precision/recall for anomalies
paper_title: Tiny but Trusted: Efficient Vision-Language Reasoning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Xiaona Zhou, Muntasir Wahed, Tianjiao Yu, Constantin Brif, Ismini Lourentzou
